summary: Traceability to Q1-Q30 and the security-baseline note is complete and nothing contradicts a clarification. Four majors: the identifier shape (one free-form field vs email vs username vs separate fields) is an unresolved product decision mislabelled as non-blocking and needs the requester; three ACs offer alternative outcomes and are not testable. Minors on unflagged elaborations and AC precision. Proposed items 1,3,5,6,8,9,10,11 are acceptable low-risk elaborations, 4 is an SDD-level default, 7 is acceptable with a clearer confirmation, 2 hangs on the identifier decision.

findings.message: HUMAN DECISION NEEDED. The identifier shape is unresolved: Q14 answer (a) is worded email (or username) and the requester never chose between them. Treating it as one free-form field is a product decision that fixes the data model, whether email syntax is validated, the sign-up/login labels, and whether case-insensitive uniqueness (REQ-AUTH-001 AC-6) is standard (email) or a choice (username). The Open questions section says None that block the spec and in the next sentence asks for an answer before freeze, which is self-contradictory and conflicts with CLAUDE.md rule 5 (ambiguous: ask, never guess).
findings.suggestion: Raise it to @alokkulkarni as Q31 (options: email only; username only; one free-form field accepting either; separate email and username fields) and record the answer in clarifications.md, then update the Glossary (L26), REQ-AUTH-001 and REQ-AUTH-002; at minimum list it as a blocking open question for the freeze approver and drop None that block.

findings.message: REQ-ISO-001 AC-2 allows two outcomes, refused as not found (or forbidden), so no single test or API contract can be written against it.
findings.suggestion: Pick one; not found is consistent with the existence-hiding rationale already used in REQ-AUTH-002 AC-3.

findings.message: REQ-LIST-003 AC-6 offers alternatives at both layers: the API returns an empty page with the total (or a validation error), and the UI shows the last valid page or the empty state. The criterion is not deterministic and cannot be tested as written.
findings.suggestion: Choose one API behaviour (for example an empty page with the correct total count) and one UI behaviour (for example navigate to the last valid page), keeping the proposed marker.

findings.message: REQ-TODO-007 AC-4 says the action is disabled or does nothing harmful; does nothing harmful is not observable and the two alternatives need different tests.
findings.suggestion: State one behaviour, for example: the Clear all completed control is disabled in the UI, and the API call with no completed to-dos succeeds deleting 0 items with no error.

findings.message: A valid identifier is defined only as non-empty: no maximum length, format (email syntax or not) or allowed characters; the password has a proposed minimum but no maximum. REQ-AUTH-001 AC-1 and AC-3 therefore cannot cover invalid non-empty input.
findings.suggestion: Once F-1 is answered, add identifier format and length rules and a password maximum length as ACs (marked proposed where not stated by the requester).

findings.message: REQ-TODO-004 AC-1 lets the user edit due date and priority, but its only trace is Q7, which covers title/description and predates Q16. A reasonable elaboration, but unflagged; clearing the optional description on edit is also not stated.
findings.suggestion: Trace to Q7 and Q16 (or mark the due date/priority editing as proposed) and add whether the description can be cleared on edit.

findings.message: REQ-TODO-001 AC-2 is UI-framed (Given I do not choose a priority); it does not say the API applies Medium when priority is omitted, so the server-side default is untested.
findings.suggestion: State that a create request with no priority is stored with priority Medium, for both UI and API.

findings.message: Clear all completed deletes across all pages, filters and search (AC-2, proposed), but the confirmation in AC-1 only says they will be deleted permanently; a user viewing a search result could expect only the visible items to go.
findings.suggestion: Require the confirmation to state the number of completed to-dos to be deleted and that it covers all completed to-dos, not only those shown.

findings.message: REQ-TODO-005 AC-2 (mark not done) does not say the updated timestamp advances, while AC-1 and REQ-TODO-004 AC-1 do; the rule is inconsistent.
findings.suggestion: Add that marking not done persists and advances the updated timestamp.

findings.message: REQ-TODO-005 AC-3 says the to-do leaves the Active view on the next refresh of the list, which does not say whether that is immediate after the toggle or only after a manual reload.
findings.suggestion: State the observable timing, for example: the list re-queries after the toggle and the to-do is no longer shown in the Active view.

findings.message: NFR-004 AC-2 (server-side validation, no stack traces or SQL errors) and AC-3 (no committed secrets) go beyond the security-baseline note, which covers only password hashing, and are neither traced nor marked proposed.
findings.suggestion: Trace AC-3 to CLAUDE.md rule 10 and mark AC-2 as a security baseline elaboration (or proposed).

findings.message: Sign-up AC-2 reveals that an identifier is taken, so the non-enumeration goal of REQ-AUTH-002 AC-3 is only partial. Acceptable for a local-only first release, but it should be recorded as an accepted trade-off so the security review does not read it as a contradiction.
findings.suggestion: Add a note under REQ-AUTH-002 AC-3 that sign-up necessarily discloses identifier existence and that this is accepted.

findings.message: Assessment of the Proposed list: items 1 (password min 8), 3 (generic login error, really security baseline), 5 (logout), 6 (past due dates), 8 (search literals/whitespace), 9 (pagination edges, once F-3 is fixed), 10 (DB auto-create) and 11 (quantified feels instant; 1 s is loose but testable) are acceptable low-risk elaborations; 4 (8 h session) is an engineering default the SDD can own; 7 (clear-all scope) is acceptable with F-8; 2 (case-insensitive uniqueness) depends on F-1 and goes to the requester with it. All still need confirmation by the freeze approver.
findings.suggestion: Split the list into product decisions for the requester (identifier, case rule) and engineering defaults for the SDD, so the approver sees only what is theirs.

findings.message: Out of scope does not mention sorting by due date or priority, although the Q24 option text mentioned sorting by priority; only newest-first ordering was requested (Q9).
findings.suggestion: Add user-selectable sorting (by due date or priority) to Out of scope.
